articles.author: Northwind Air Media Relations
articles.title: Northwind Air firms up order for 24 Meridian M-220 aircraft
articles.summary: Northwind Air has converted its memorandum of understanding into a firm order for 24 Meridian M-220 narrowbodies, with options for a further 12, to replace its ageing regional jets from 2028.
body: Northwind Air today confirmed a firm order for 24 Meridian M-220 single-aisle aircraft, converting the memorandum of understanding signed at the spring air show. The agreement includes purchase rights for a further 12 aircraft, which the carrier may exercise up to 2030.

Deliveries are scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2028 and run at roughly one aircraft per month. The M-220s will replace Northwind's fleet of 31 regional jets on its densest domestic routes, adding around 40 seats per departure while cutting fuel burn per seat by an estimated 18 percent.

"Upgauging is the fastest way for us to grow in slot-constrained airports," said chief executive Helena Marsh. "The M-220 gives us the range to open thinner international routes from our secondary bases without taking a widebody risk."

The carrier selected the Halvorsen HX-35 engine for the fleet and has signed a ten-year maintenance agreement covering shop visits and spare engine support. Financing will combine sale-and-leaseback for the first eight aircraft with export credit support for the remainder.

Northwind said the order does not change its capital expenditure guidance for 2027, as pre-delivery payments are spread across the delivery stream. The airline will provide an updated fleet plan at its capital markets day in November.

articles.author: Northwind Air Media Relations
articles.title: Northwind Air to launch three transatlantic routes for summer 2027
articles.summary: New seasonal services from Lakeshore International to Lisbon, Dublin and Reykjavik will use reconfigured long-range narrowbodies.
body: Northwind Air will open three seasonal transatlantic routes from its Lakeshore International hub in summer 2027, the airline announced, marking its first scheduled flying across the Atlantic.

Services to Lisbon and Dublin will operate four times weekly from late May, while Reykjavik will be served three times weekly between June and September. All three routes will be flown by long-range narrowbodies reconfigured with 16 lie-flat seats in a premium cabin.

The launch places Northwind in direct competition with two network carriers on the Dublin route, where it intends to compete on connecting traffic to secondary cities in its domestic network rather than on point-to-point fares.

Commercial director Ravi Okafor said advance bookings for the summer schedule were tracking ahead of plan and that the airline expected premium cabin load factors above 70 percent in the first season. Northwind is in talks with a European partner about codeshare access beyond the three gateways.
The routes are subject to final slot confirmation at Dublin, where the airline has been allocated preliminary afternoon slots.

articles.author: Dana Whitfield
articles.title: Analysis: narrowbody delivery delays keep capacity tight into 2027
articles.summary: With engine and aerostructure bottlenecks persisting, airlines are extending leases and deferring retirements; our analysis of fleet plans suggests seat growth will lag demand for another four quarters.
body: Airlines planning on a recovery in narrowbody deliveries next year should not count on it, according to fleet plans and supplier commentary reviewed by Aero Trade Weekly.

Across the twelve largest carriers in our sample, planned retirements for 2027 have been cut by nearly a third since January, as operators keep older aircraft flying to cover for late deliveries. Lease extensions on mid-life aircraft are now the default rather than the exception.

The squeeze is showing up in yields: carriers with tight capacity are reporting unit revenue growth even as fuel costs rise, while those that bet on new aircraft arriving on time are paying for wet-lease capacity to protect their schedules.

Suppliers point to forgings, castings and engine hot-section parts as the binding constraints. Two Tier 1 aerostructure suppliers told us they did not expect lead times to normalise before the second half of 2027.

For lessors, the dynamic is unambiguously positive. Lease rates for current-generation narrowbodies have risen for six consecutive quarters, and used serviceable engine values remain near record highs.

articles.author: Marcus Lindqvist
articles.title: Q3 traffic: transatlantic yields soften as capacity returns
articles.summary: Third-quarter traffic results show transatlantic load factors holding near 87 percent, but average fares slipped for the first time in two years as carriers added seats.
body: Third-quarter traffic results published over the past fortnight point to a turn in the transatlantic market. Load factors held up well, averaging around 87 percent across the carriers that report the route group separately, but average fares fell year on year for the first time since 2024.

Capacity across the North Atlantic rose about 7 percent in the quarter as long-haul aircraft returned from heavy maintenance and new narrowbody routes opened. Premium cabins remained resilient; the softness was concentrated in economy fares booked inside 30 days.

Domestic markets told a different story. With narrowbody deliveries still running late, short-haul capacity grew less than 2 percent, and unit revenues on domestic networks rose for the fifth straight quarter.

Analysts expect the divergence to persist into the winter. Several carriers have signalled that they will trim off-peak transatlantic frequencies and redeploy aircraft to leisure markets in the Caribbean and Latin America, where demand has been firmer.

articles.author: Meridian Communications
articles.title: Meridian lifts M-220 production to nine aircraft a month
articles.summary: Meridian Aerostructures has stepped up M-220 final assembly to nine aircraft per month and reaffirmed its target of twelve by the end of 2027, while flagging titanium forging capacity as the main risk.
body: Meridian Aerostructures said it has raised the production rate of its M-220 single-aisle programme to nine aircraft per month, up from seven at the start of the year, following the opening of a second final assembly line.

The company reaffirmed its plan to reach twelve aircraft per month by the end of 2027, but cautioned that titanium forgings for the wing-to-body fittings remain the programme's tightest constraint. Meridian has qualified a second forging supplier and is funding additional press capacity at an existing supplier.

Engine availability has improved, the company said, with Halvorsen delivering HX-35 engines in line with the airframe schedule for three consecutive months. Meridian had 14 completed airframes awaiting engines at the end of the second quarter; that number has fallen to four.
The M-220 backlog stands at 1,140 aircraft after recent orders, including the firm commitment from Northwind Air. At the planned rate, the backlog represents more than seven years of production.

articles.author: Meridian Investor Relations
articles.title: Meridian reports third-quarter results: 61 deliveries, positive free cash flow
articles.summary: Meridian Aerostructures delivered 61 aircraft in the third quarter, generated positive free cash flow for the first time this year and narrowed its full-year delivery guidance.
body: Meridian Aerostructures reported revenue of 9.8 billion for the third quarter, up 14 percent year on year, on 61 commercial aircraft deliveries. Free cash flow was positive at 410 million, reversing an outflow in the first half as inventory of unfinished airframes was worked down.

The company narrowed its full-year delivery guidance to between 235 and 245 aircraft, from a previous range of 230 to 260, citing steadier engine supply offset by continued delays in cabin interiors for widebody customers.

Operating margin in the commercial segment improved to 7.9 percent. Meridian took a charge of 120 million on its regional turboprop programme, where it is renegotiating supplier contracts after lower than expected order intake.

Chief financial officer Priya Raman said the company expected abnormal costs from supply chain disruption to decline through 2027 as rate increases stabilise. Order intake in the quarter was 96 aircraft, for a book-to-bill ratio of 1.6.

articles.author: Certification Directorate
articles.title: Airworthiness directive mandates repeat fan blade inspections on HX-35 engines
articles.summary: An emergency airworthiness directive requires ultrasonic inspection of HX-35 fan blades within 50 flight cycles after a blade root crack was found during a scheduled shop visit.
body: The certification directorate has issued an emergency airworthiness directive applicable to Halvorsen HX-35 turbofan engines with fan blades from three specified production batches.

The directive follows the discovery of a crack at the root of a fan blade during a scheduled shop visit. Investigation has so far attributed the finding to a deviation in the shot-peening process at a sub-tier supplier. No in-flight event has been reported.

Operators must perform an ultrasonic inspection of affected blades within 50 flight cycles of the directive's effective date, and repeat the inspection every 400 flight cycles thereafter until the blades are replaced. Blades with indications above the stated threshold must be removed before further flight.

The engine manufacturer estimates that around 380 engines in service are affected. Each on-wing inspection takes approximately six hours. Operators with large affected fleets have been advised to plan inspections at overnight maintenance stations to limit schedule disruption.
The directive will be reviewed once the root cause investigation is complete; a terminating action through blade replacement is expected.

articles.author: Environmental Protection Unit
articles.title: Consultation opens on sustainable aviation fuel reporting rules
articles.summary: A public consultation proposes harmonised reporting of sustainable aviation fuel uplift by airport, with fuel suppliers and aircraft operators submitting data quarterly from 2027.
body: A twelve-week public consultation has opened on draft rules for reporting the uplift of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) under the regional blending mandate.

The proposal would require fuel suppliers to report SAF volumes delivered at each airport every quarter, and aircraft operators to report the fuel uplifted per airport annually. The two data sets would be reconciled to detect double counting of book-and-claim certificates.

Industry groups have argued for a single annual report to reduce administrative cost. The draft rejects that approach, saying quarterly data is needed to monitor whether supply is concentrated at a few hub airports, which would undermine the mandate's goal of broad availability.
The consultation also asks for views on penalties for operators that tanker conventional fuel to avoid uplifting at airports where SAF is blended at higher cost. Responses are due by mid-January.

articles.author: Tomas Brandt
articles.title: Engine shop turnaround stretches past 120 days as parts shortages bite
articles.summary: Average turnaround for narrowbody engine performance restorations has risen to about 125 days, roughly double pre-2020 norms, with high-pressure turbine parts the most common cause of delay.
body: Turnaround times for narrowbody engine performance restorations have climbed to an average of about 125 days, according to shop operators and lessors, roughly twice what airlines planned for before 2020.

The single largest cause is the availability of high-pressure turbine blades and vanes. Several independent shops said they are holding engines that are otherwise complete while waiting for one or two hot-section parts. Used serviceable material has filled part of the gap, but prices for overhauled blades have risen sharply.
The newly mandated fan blade inspections on HX-35 engines are expected to add to the pressure, as some operators choose to bring forward shop visits rather than repeat on-wing checks.

Lessors report that spare engine utilisation is near 100 percent, and short-term spare engine lease rates have risen by around 40 percent over the past year. Airlines are responding by pooling spares and negotiating priority slots in their maintenance agreements.

articles.author: Tomas Brandt
articles.title: Lessors extend leases as mid-life engine values keep climbing
articles.summary: Extensions now account for most narrowbody lease transactions, and the market value of mid-life engines has overtaken the value of the airframes they are installed on.
body: Lease extensions now make up the majority of narrowbody lease transactions, lessors said, as airlines keep aircraft they had planned to return in order to cover for late new deliveries.

Mid-life engine values have continued to rise, and for several current-generation types the two engines are now worth more than the airframe. That has made part-out economics attractive for older aircraft, but lessors said they are reluctant to retire airframes that airlines are willing to lease.

Extension terms have shortened, with three-year extensions replacing the five-year terms common before 2020, and rates have been set closer to new-lease levels. Return conditions are being relaxed in some deals in exchange for higher rent.

articles.author: Grace Ng
articles.title: Lakeshore International approves 1.4 billion terminal expansion
articles.summary: The operator of Lakeshore International has approved a pier extension and new security hall, adding capacity for eight million annual passengers by 2030.
body: The board of Lakeshore International Airport has approved a 1.4 billion programme to extend its north pier and build a consolidated security hall, raising the airport's annual capacity from 24 million to 32 million passengers.

Construction will begin next spring and the first six contact stands are expected to open in 2029. The project is being financed through a combination of a bond issue and an increase in passenger charges, which airlines had opposed during consultation.

Northwind Air, which accounts for about 45 percent of traffic at Lakeshore, said it supported the expansion but would continue to challenge the level of the charge increase with the regulator. The airline's new transatlantic services will use the existing south pier until the extension opens.
The operator said the design reserves space for an airport-wide sustainable aviation fuel hydrant connection, in anticipation of blending obligations.

articles.author: Grace Ng
articles.title: Air traffic controller shortages drove a third of summer delays
articles.summary: A review of summer operations attributes about a third of en-route delay minutes to staffing constraints at four area control centres.
body: Staffing shortages at four area control centres accounted for roughly a third of en-route delay minutes this summer, according to a review of operations published by the network manager.
Average en-route delay per flight rose to 2.1 minutes, against a target of 0.9. Weather contributed most of the remainder, with an unusually active convective season in July.

Airlines have called for faster training pipelines and for capacity to be shared across borders when one centre is short-staffed. The network manager said cross-border sectorisation trials will be extended next summer.
Airports reported knock-on effects on ground operations, with aircraft held at stands increasing taxi times and missed connections at hub airports.

articles.author: Pressestelle Flughafen Nordhafen
articles.title: Flughafen Nordhafen: Passagierzahlen im September deutlich über Vorjahr
articles.summary: Im September nutzten 1,9 Millionen Fluggäste den Flughafen Nordhafen, ein Plus von 9 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahresmonat.
body: Der Flughafen Nordhafen hat im September rund 1,9 Millionen Passagiere abgefertigt, neun Prozent mehr als im Vorjahresmonat. Damit lag das Aufkommen erstmals seit 2019 über dem damaligen Niveau.

Getragen wurde das Wachstum vor allem vom Urlaubsverkehr in den Mittelmeerraum sowie von neuen Verbindungen nach Nordamerika. Die Zahl der Flugbewegungen stieg dagegen nur um drei Prozent, da die Fluggesellschaften größere Flugzeuge einsetzten und die Auslastung erhöhten.
Das Frachtaufkommen ging um vier Prozent zurück. Die Flughafengesellschaft führt dies auf geringere Kapazitäten im Unterdeck von Passagierflugzeugen auf Asienstrecken zurück.
Für das Gesamtjahr rechnet der Flughafen nun mit etwa 20 Millionen Fluggästen und hebt seine Prognose damit leicht an.

articles.author: Innovation Unit
articles.title: Beyond-visual-line-of-sight drone corridor trial extended to two more regions
articles.summary: The trial of a shared airspace corridor for beyond-visual-line-of-sight drone deliveries will be extended to two further regions after six months without a separation incident.
